records.text: Candace Owens said the People's Will terrorist group plotted the assassination of Tsar Alexander II.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It was plotted by a terrorist group in Russia known in English as the People's Will. That was the name of the terrorist group.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Library of Congress historical material identifies Narodnaya Volya (People’s Will) as the revolutionary organization responsible for the 1881 assassination of Alexander II after repeated plots.

sources.title: Narodnaya Volya (People’s Will) – Library of Congress
sources.relevance: Confirms the organization and its role in the assassination of Alexander II.

records.text: Candace Owens said Jewish people were about four percent of the population but were overrepresented in the People's Will cell involved in Alexander II's assassination.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And despite the fact, and these again are facts, that Jewish people represented only 4% of the population, they were overrepresented in this terrorist cell. ... That was involved in the plotting and the eventual assassination of the Tsar in 1880 in 1881, which is when his carriage was passing through St.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The Russian Empire’s Jewish population was roughly four percent, while scholarship documents disproportionate participation by Jewish women in revolutionary circles. The wording risks implying collective responsibility; participation by individual Jews does not implicate Jews as a group.

sources.title: Dangerous Politics, Dangerous Liaisons: Love and Terror among Jewish Women Revolutionaries – Deborah Hertz
sources.relevance: Supports disproportionate participation of Jewish women in late-imperial revolutionary movements.

sources.title: Pale of Settlement – YIVO Encyclopedia
sources.relevance: Provides demographic and legal context for Jews in the Russian Empire.

records.text: Candace Owens said the Church of the Savior on Spilled Blood was built where Alexander II's carriage was bombed.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Petersburg, and I'm going to show you a video that I shot right in the spot where the bomb was thrown on him. ... The church is called, appropriately, called the Church of the Savior on Spilled Blood, and this is a video so you guys can see that's where his carriage was bombed.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The Church of the Savior on Spilled Blood was built on the site where Alexander II was mortally wounded by a bomb in March 1881.

sources.title: Church of the Savior on Spilled Blood – Visit Petersburg
sources.relevance: Official destination history confirms the church’s construction at the assassination site.
